newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK interbank rates ease on tame US inflation data.
newsitem.headline: HK interbank rates ease on tame US inflation data.

text.p: Interbank rates were lower on increased liquidity following the two injections made by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority earlier this week and cautious sentiment resulting from tame U.S. inflation data, dealers said on Friday.
The overnight eased to 5-1/8 five from 5-3/16 1/16 percent on Thursday and three-month money was 5-5/8 1/2 against 5-11/16 9/16 percent.

Some local traders believed the Federal Reserve was unlikely to raise interest rates in September after the release of the weaker-than-expected U.S. producer price data. "The long-dated U.S. bond yields should continue to fall," one said.
Others, however, were waiting for Friday night's U.S. August consumer price and retail sales data.
Government paper rose in line with U.S. Treasurys.
"The yield curve of Exchange Fund bills and notes fell by five basis points on average," one dealer said.
The one-week bill yield was 4.93 against 4.96 percent. Seven-year Exchange Fund note yielded 7.73 vs 7.79, five-year 7.33 vs 7.40 nad three-year 6.75 vs 6.80.
